cases.title: Plane wall: fixed temperature on one face, convection on the other, other faces insulated
cases.reference: Analytic 1D conduction in series with convection (Incropera, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, section 3.1, thermal resistance network): q = (T0 - Tinf) / (L/k + 1/h) with k 2 W/m K, L 20 mm, h 10 W/m2K, T0 100 C, Tinf 20 C gives Q = 0.07272727 W through 10 x 10 mm. The profile is exactly linear, so the cell-centre values are exact too: 92.90909 C in the cell at the convective face, 99.81818 C at the fixed face. Tolerances only cover the iterative solver.

calls.metric: T at the convective face cell
T at the fixed face cell

cases.title: Same plane wall, voxel size 3 mm that does not divide the 20 x 10 x 10 mm bar (7 x 4 x 4 voxels)
cases.reference: Analytic 1D conduction in series with convection as in slab-1d-convection (Incropera section 3.1): Q = 0.07272727 W. With h = 3 mm the conservative voxelizer keeps the partly touched last voxel in every axis (21 x 12 x 12 mm), which would add 2.5 % to Q without the staircase correction of the conduction path (face conductances and half-cell resistances scaled per axis by (V/V_voxel)(E_voxel/E)^2, as the film area already is). Tolerance 1 % of Q (stated before running; the uncorrected error was 2.5 % at h = 3 mm and 4.4 % at 7 mm).

cases.title: Plane wall with uniform heat generation and convection on both faces
cases.reference: Analytic (Incropera section 3.5, plane wall with uniform generation, same h and Tinf both sides): T(x) = Tinf + q'''L/h + q''' (L^2 - x^2)/(2k), half thickness L 10 mm, k 2, h 10, q''' 100000 W/m3 (P = 0.2 W in 20 x 10 x 10 mm), Tinf 20 C. At the cell centre x = 0.5 mm: 122.49375 C. Cell-centred finite volume is second order, so the profile is matched to a small fraction of a kelvin, not to solver precision; all of P leaves by convection (energy conservation, exact).

cases.title: Long cylinder with uniform heat generation, convection on the curved surface, insulated ends
cases.reference: Analytic (Incropera section 3.5, radial system with uniform generation): T(r) = Ts + q''' (R^2 - r^2)/(4k), Ts = Tinf + q''' R/(2h), R 10 mm, k 1, h 100, Tinf 20 C, P = 2 W in a 10 mm length (q''' = 6.3662e+5 W/m3, power per length 200 W/m). At r = 0.354 mm (the voxel nearest the axis): rise 47.7266 K. The kernel's 48-gon is within 0.3 % of the circle in area and 0.1 % in perimeter. Staircase surface: the film conductance is scaled so each body keeps its mesh surface area. The metric is the absolute temperature at the axis voxel (340.877 K = 293.15 K + the rise). Tolerance 2 % of the rise (0.955 K, 0.28 % of the temperature shown), stated before running.

calls.metric: T at the axis (rise above ambient 47.73 K)

cases.title: Straight rectangular fin with a convective tip: efficiency
cases.reference: Analytic (Incropera section 3.6, rectangular fin, convection from the tip, eq. 3.72 and 3.91): q_f = M (sinh mL + (h/mk) cosh mL)/(cosh mL + (h/mk) sinh mL), M = sqrt(h P k Ac) theta_b, m = sqrt(h P/(k Ac)); eta_f = q_f/(h A_f theta_b). Fin 100 x 10 x 2 mm, k 167 W/m K (aluminium), h 25 W/m2K, base 100 C, ambient 20 C: m 13.403 1/m, mL 1.340, q_f 3.13148 W, A_f 2420 mm2, eta 0.64700. The 1D formula neglects the temperature variation across the 2 mm thickness (Biot 1.5e-4), so 3D and 1D agree; tolerance 1 % covers discretisation. Efficiency is computed as q_f / (h A_f theta_b) from the heat leaving through the fixed base.

cases.title: Lumped-capacitance heating of a 20 mm aluminium cube (Biot 5e-4)
cases.reference: Analytic (Incropera section 5.1, lumped capacitance with generation): T - Tinf = (P/(hA)) (1 - exp(-t/tau)), tau = rho cp V/(h A) = 322.560 s, Bi = hV/(A k) = 4.99e-4 (lumped to better than 0.1 %). Cube 20 mm, aluminium k 167 rho 2700 cp 896, h 25 W/m2K on all faces, P = 4.800 W (steady rise 80 K), starting at Tinf 20 C. Volume-mean temperature at 600 s: 87.5477 C; time to reach 70 C: 316.38 s. First-order time stepping (implicit Euler, 1 s step) contributes about 0.04 K by the first-order estimate (t/tau)(dt/2tau)exp(-t/tau) x 80 K (0.014 K measured); the temperature tolerance of 0.15 K (0.2 % of the 80 K rise) also covers the voxel volume-mean approximation, and the time tolerance is 1 %. Limits are stated before running.

cases.title: Plane wall suddenly held at a fixed surface temperature (transient conduction)
cases.reference: Analytic (Incropera section 5.5, exact one-term-per-eigenvalue solution, plane wall with surface temperature step): theta* = sum_n C_n exp(-zeta_n^2 Fo) cos(zeta_n x/L), zeta_n = (2n-1) pi/2, C_n = 4 (-1)^(n+1)/((2n-1) pi), 200 terms. Wall 20 mm (L = 10 mm), k 1, rho 1000, cp 1000 (alpha 0.000001 m2/s), initially 100 C, both faces 20 C from t = 0. At t = 50 s (Fo 0.50) and x = 0.5 mm from the mid-plane: 49.5708 C. Implicit Euler with a 0.1 s step and 0.5 mm cells; tolerance 0.3 K (1 % of the 29.6 K remaining difference), stated before running.

cases.title: Block with a heat source and a contact conductance to a sink on one face, everything else insulated
cases.reference: Analytic 1D: heat q''' (L - x) flows toward the contact face at x = 0, so T(x) = Tinf + q''' L/h_c + q''' (L x - x^2/2)/k with q''' = P/(A L) = 249999.99999999997 W/m3 (P 0.5 W, 10 x 10 x 20 mm), k 2, L 20 mm, contact h_c 500 W/m2K to a sink at 20 C (a mount with conductance_W_m2K, as in Analyze > Mounts). At the first cell centre (x = 0.25 mm): 30.6211 C; at the last (x = 19.75 mm): 54.9961 C. All P leaves through the contact (exact).

cases.title: Aluminium cube heated in still air with radiation only (iterated linearisation)
cases.reference: Exact balance: P = eps sigma A (Ts^4 - Ta^4) (Stefan-Boltzmann, grey surface in large surroundings; Incropera eq. 1.7 and 1.9), A = 24 cm2, eps 0.9, P 1 W, Ta 293.15 K gives Ts = 353.1269 K. The cube is isothermal to 0.037 K at most (conduction, k 167), so the centre cell is within 0.2 K of Ts; the solver linearises h_r = eps sigma (Ts^2 + Ta^2)(Ts + Ta) and iterates it with the face temperature.

cases.title: Copper block with the outer size of the sealed box of Cengel Example 15-10, 112.7 W
cases.reference: Cengel, Heat and Mass Transfer 3rd ed., Example 15-10 (free chapter 15): box 0.40 x 0.30 x 0.15 m, eps 0.85, bottom insulated, room 35 C: published heat loss 112.7 W at a surface temperature of 65 C (convection 48.2 W, radiation 64.5 W). Here a solid copper block (k 401, isothermal to a few tenths of a kelvin) of that size receives 112.7 W through the Analyze conditions and the solver finds its surface temperature with the A1 correlations. Heat flows are about +-15 % from correlation spread (A1 reports 15 % on convection, 8 % on the total), which is about +-3.6 K on the 30 K rise (rise ~ Q^(1/1.25): 30 (1.15^0.8 - 1) = 3.5 K), so the tolerance is 3.6 K around 65 C. Not independent evidence for A2: the solver uses A1's own correlations (copied into the voxel core), so this is a plumbing check of the 3D model against a book value that those correlations already approximate.

cases.title: Enclosure with a board and a 1 W part: every watt leaves (steady)
cases.reference: Conservation of energy (exact): at steady state the heat leaving through convection, radiation and contacts equals the 1 W dissipated; the balance is evaluated with the boundary coefficients recomputed at the final temperatures, so it also measures the nonlinear iteration. Not a comparison with a measurement.

cases.title: Same enclosure, transient: heat in = heat out + heat stored
cases.reference: Conservation of energy (exact): at every implicit-Euler step C (T_new - T_old)/dt + Q_out = Q_in with the coefficients the step used; the reported error is the last step, in watts. 300 s from ambient in 5 s steps.

cases.title: Enclosure 1: 60 x 40 x 25 mm ABS case, 2 mm wall, 1 W part on a board, still air 25 C
cases.reference: Spec docs/EXTENSIONS_SPEC.md section 4 (A1 validation): A1, the resistance network, and A2, the 3D finite-volume solution, should agree within 15 % on the hottest-part temperature RISE above ambient for three reference enclosures. A1 is the reference side only in the sense of the spec: neither is a measurement. Sealed small box, thick plastic wall, no mount.

cases.title: Enclosure 2: 140 x 70 x 30 mm polycarbonate case, 3 W SoC and 1 W regulator, still air 30 C
cases.reference: Spec docs/EXTENSIONS_SPEC.md section 4 (A1 validation): A1, the resistance network, and A2, the 3D finite-volume solution, should agree within 15 % on the hottest-part temperature RISE above ambient for three reference enclosures. A1 is the reference side only in the sense of the spec: neither is a measurement. Larger plastic hand-held case with two heat sources.
cases.expectedDivergence: Documented expected divergence, tolerance NOT loosened: A2 gives a rise 20.8 % above A1 (A2 129.2 C vs A1 112.1 C at the time of writing). The cause is not isolated: A1 is a resistance network without board spreading and with its own cavity model, A2 treats the enclosed air as an effective conductor (called coarse in its warnings), and neither is a measurement. The case stays red as a check and does not count as a pass; the Elmer reference of step A4 is the arbiter.

cases.title: Enclosure 3: 100 x 60 x 30 mm aluminium case, 5 W part, rail-mount contact 150 W/m2K on the bottom, 25 C
cases.reference: Spec docs/EXTENSIONS_SPEC.md section 4 (A1 validation): A1, the resistance network, and A2, the 3D finite-volume solution, should agree within 15 % on the hottest-part temperature RISE above ambient for three reference enclosures. A1 is the reference side only in the sense of the spec: neither is a measurement. Conductive metal case with a contact to a sink.

cases.title: 3D enclosure against an Elmer reference, max-temperature error within 5 % at fine
cases.reference: Spec docs/EXTENSIONS_SPEC.md section 4 (A2 validation): "a 3D enclosure compared with an Elmer reference within 5 % max-temperature error at fine". The reference numbers are produced once by the Alloy Runner (step A4) with Elmer and stored in analysis-validation/reference/enclosure-elmer.json (format in analysis-validation/README.md). That file does not exist yet, so this case is SKIPPED: it is not a pass, and A2 therefore returns validity "estimate".
